what:
**Round-4 user audit corrections (2026-04-28):**

1. **Telemetry default is ON** (resolves the running confusion). User said "telemetry is opted in by default with aide telemetry on always" + previously "how would default be off." Both rounds the user has been pushing back on the opt-in / default-off framing. Resolution: flip code state + docs back to default-ON. Memory #202 was the original direction; memory #373 flipped to opt-in; user is now flipping back. Going with the most recent direction: ON by default. Code change in `src/memory/analytics.ts`: `POSTHOG_KEY` should ship unconditionally and only short-circuit on `AIDE_TELEMETRY=off`. Docs say: "Telemetry is on by default. Disable by setting `AIDE_TELEMETRY=off`. When on, only anonymized event counts are sent (no content, no paths, no queries)." This supersedes memory #373's flip.

2. **Cross-tool framing: project context, not session/conversation context.** User: "its more about project context." The honest claim: the memory store (your project's captured context) goes across tools and teammates. Don't frame the negative ("conversation context belongs to the tool") because that muddies. Just say: "Memories are tied to your project, not to whatever tool you're using to talk to the agent. Switch from Claude Code to Cursor (or vice versa) and your project's memory store is right there." Drop "conversation context still belongs to the tool" entirely.

3. **Manual capture vs manual recall — the actual problem.** My round-3 framing "Capture exists, but recall doesn't auto-fire without another tool" was wrong. User: "I mean like manual capture and recall is what the problem is but we have automatic of each." So the real problem aide-memory addresses: with rules files you do manual capture AND manual recall (the agent has to be told to consider the rules; rules don't auto-fire on relevant files). With aide-memory, BOTH are automated: hooks prompt for capture on corrections/decisions, hooks prompt for recall when the agent opens a file with scoped memories. The differentiator is automating BOTH ends, not "recall doesn't auto-fire."

4. **Free framing: keep it simple, drop the qualifications.** User: "just make it free with future editions coming, keep it simple." Replace any version of "Free for individuals today. Future enhancements may stay free, or some may ship as separate tiers as the project grows. No promises either way" with: **"Free. More features coming."** or **"Free to use. More coming."** That's it. No tier-promising, no caveat, no "for individuals," no "as the project grows."

5. **Tagline "Memory that travels." — user doesn't love it.** Workshop again. Constraint: short, no overclaim. Options to consider: "Memory that grows with your codebase." / "The memory layer for your codebase and team." / "Persistent memory for your codebase." / "Captured. Scoped. Shared." / Just "Persistent memory for AI coding agents and teams" without any trailing tagline. Pick something less abstract than "travels."

6. **Spacing: split diff between previous and current.** User wants me to show the BEFORE/AFTER values for spacing changes (e.g. CSS padding) instead of describing them abstractly. Apply this same format to all sentence-level changes going forward.

**Format directive for change-log tables (most important process change):**
- The previous round's table used phrases like "reframed as X," "reworded to Y," "section split into 6," etc. User explicitly: "I dont want reframed I want actual showing sentence by sentence what you changed."
- Going forward: every line in a change-log table is **BEFORE** literal text → **AFTER** literal text. For mechanical changes (em-dash strip, default value change, link path replacement), say "mechanical: X → Y throughout file Z." For new sections added, show the literal new heading + first line.
- This applies to every future round of doc-rewrite reporting.

Without these as durable rules, the same misframings come back: "core engine stays free for solo developers," "switch tools mid-task and context follows," "default opt-in by default," and reports that summarize instead of show.
why: Round-4 audit lands very specific corrections that must stick: telemetry default is ON (user has now flipped this twice; finalizing here), cross-tool framing is about project context not conversation context, the rules-files problem is "manual capture AND manual recall" not "recall doesn't auto-fire," free framing should be one sentence not three, and reporting must show literal sentence-by-sentence diffs not abstract reframings. Stored as priority:always so future doc-edit sessions don't slip back into any of the above. Supersedes #373 on telemetry default.
